parts.latex:
The life span of batteries from a particular factory is normally distributed with a mean of 840 hours and a standard deviation of 80 hours.

It is known from statistical tables that for this distribution approximately $60\%$ of the batteries have a life span of less than 860 hours.

What is the approximate percentage of batteries with a life span between 820 and 920 hours?

solutions.latex:
\exfigure{271_q37_s1}

Since $60\%$ have a life span below 860 hours and $50\%$ are below the mean of 840:

$10\%$ have a life span between 840 and 860.

By symmetry, $10\%$ have a life span between 820 and 840.

The interval 760 to 920 is within 1 standard deviation of the mean, so $68\%$ lie in it.

Hence $34\%$ have a life span between 840 and 920.

Therefore the percentage between 820 and 920 hours is
$$10\% + 34\% = 44\%$$

4513.stem:
The Intelligence Quotient (IQ) scores for adults in City $A$ are normally distributed with a mean of 108 and a standard deviation of 10.

The IQ scores for adults in City $B$ are normally distributed with a mean of 112 and a standard deviation of 16.

parts.latex:
Yin is an adult who lives in City $A$ and has an IQ score of 128.

What percentage of the adults in this city have an IQ score higher than Yin's?

There are 1 000 000 adults living in City $B$.

Calculate the number of adults in City $B$ that would be expected to have an IQ score lower than Yin's.

Simon, an adult who lives in City $A$, moves to City $B$. The $z$-score corresponding to his IQ score in City $A$ is the same as the $z$-score corresponding to his IQ score in City $B$.

By first forming an equation, calculate Simon's IQ score. Give your answer correct to one decimal place.

solutions.latex:
$$\dfrac{128-108}{10} = 2$$
So $128$ is 2 standard deviations above the mean.

About $95\%$ of scores lie within 2 standard deviations, so $5\%$ lie outside, split equally between the two tails.
$$\therefore\ \dfrac{5\%}{2} = 2.5\% \text{ have an IQ score higher than Yin's}$$
criteria: Demonstrates that $97.5\%$ relates to 2 standard deviations above the mean, or equivalent merit

meta.final_by: claude-sonnet-5-5 26 Nov (read from the worked solution)

solutions.latex:
Mean of City $B$ is $112$, so one standard deviation above the mean is
$$112+16 = 128$$
So Yin's score is 1 standard deviation above the mean in City $B$.

The percentage with a lower score is
$$50\%+\dfrac{1}{2}\times 68\% = 84\%$$
The expected number of adults is
$$1\,000\,000\times 0.84 = 840\,000$$
criteria: Demonstrates Yin is 1 standard deviation above the mean in City $B$, or equivalent merit

meta.final_by: claude-sonnet-5-5 26 Nov (read from the worked solution)

solutions.latex:
Let $x$ be Simon's IQ score. Using $z=\dfrac{x-\mu}{\sigma}$:
$$\begin{aligned} z_A &= \dfrac{x-108}{10} \\ z_B &= \dfrac{x-112}{16} \end{aligned}$$
The $z$-scores are equal:
$$\begin{aligned} \dfrac{x-108}{10} &= \dfrac{x-112}{16} \\ 16(x-108) &= 10(x-112) \\ 16x-1728 &= 10x-1120 \\ 6x &= 608 \\ x &\approx 101.3 \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ \text{Simon's IQ score is } 101.3$$
criteria: Provides correct equation linking City $A$ with City $B$
Provides correct expression for the $z$-score for City $A$ or City $B$, or equivalent merit

parts.latex:
The weight of boxes of cereal that are produced in a factory are normally distributed with a mean of 650 grams and a standard deviation of 5 grams.

Boxes of cereal are fit for sale if they weigh more than 640 grams.

If the factory produces one million boxes, how many would you expect to be fit for sale?

solutions.latex:
Find the $z$-score of $640$ g.
$$\begin{aligned} z &= \dfrac{640 - 650}{5} \\ &= -2 \end{aligned}$$
Using the normal distribution regions ($13.5\%$, $34\%$, $50\%$), the proportion above $640$ g is $97.5\%$.
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Number fit for sale} &= 97.5\% \times 1\,000\,000 \\ &= 975\,000 \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ 975\,000 \text{ boxes}$$

The scores on an examination are normally distributed with a mean of 70 and a standard deviation of 6. Michael received a score on the examination between the lower quartile and the upper quartile of the scores.

Which shaded region most accurately represents where Michael’s score lies?

solutions.latex:
The lower and upper quartiles cut off the bottom $25\%$ and top $25\%$, so Michael's score is in the middle $50\%$.

For a normal distribution the quartiles are about $0.67$ standard deviations from the mean.

$$\begin{aligned} Q_1 &\approx 70 - 0.67\times 6 \approx 66 \\ Q_3 &\approx 70 + 0.67\times 6 \approx 74 \end{aligned}$$

The shaded region should run from about $66$ to $74$, which is narrower than $\mu \pm \sigma$ ($64$ to $76$, about $68\%$).

Only the first graph has its shading inside the $64$ and $76$ lines, so it is option A.

parts.latex:
The minimum daily temperature, in degrees, of a town each year follows a normal distribution with its mean equal to its standard deviation. The minimum daily temperature was recorded over one year.

What percentage of the recorded minimum daily temperatures was above zero degrees?

solutions.latex:
Let the mean be $\mu$ and the standard deviation be $\sigma$, with $\mu = \sigma$.

Zero is below the mean by
$$\dfrac{\mu - 0}{\sigma} = 1 \text{ standard deviation}$$
so its $z$-score is $-1$.

By the empirical rule, $68\%$ of values lie within one standard deviation of the mean, so $34\%$ lie between $0$ and $\mu$. Also $50\%$ lie above the mean.
$$P(X > 0) = 50\% + 34\% = 84\%$$
Hence the correct option is D.

In a flock of $12\,600$ sheep, the ratio of males to females is $1 : 20$.

The weights of the male sheep are normally distributed with a mean of 76.2 kg and a standard deviation of 6.8 kg.

In the flock, 15 of the male sheep each weigh more than $x$ kg.

Find the value of $x$.

The weights of the female sheep are also normally distributed but have a smaller mean and smaller standard deviation than the weights of male sheep.

Explain whether it could be expected that 300 of the females from the flock each weigh more than $x$ kg, where $x$ is the value found in part (a).

solutions.latex:
The ratio $1:20$ gives 21 parts:
$$\text{Number of male sheep} = \dfrac{12\,600}{21} = 600$$
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Percentage of males over } x \text{ kg} &= \dfrac{15}{600} \times 100 \\ &= 2.5\% \end{aligned}$$
\exfigure{5834_q40_s1}

The top $2.5\%$ lies above $2$ standard deviations, so the $z$-score is $2$.
$$\begin{aligned} x &= 76.2 + 2 \times 6.8 \\ &= 76.2 + 13.6 \\ &= 89.8 \text{ kg} \end{aligned}$$
criteria: Attempts to use a $z$-score in a calculation, or equivalent merit
Calculates the percentage of males that weigh more than $x$ kg
Calculates the number of male sheep, or equivalent merit

solutions.latex:
For females, $z = \dfrac{x - \mu}{\sigma}$ will be larger than $2$, as the mean and standard deviation for females are smaller.

So the percentage of female sheep weighing more than $x$ kg will be smaller than $2.5\%$.

Hence fewer than 300 females will weigh more than $x$ kg.

parts.latex:
The speeds (in km/h) which are recorded on a radar device approaching a section of road work are normally distributed, with a mean of 58 and a standard deviation of 4.

The speed limit for the section is 60 km/h and 2400 vehicles passed the radar in one day.

How many vehicles were travelling at 2 km/h above the speed limit or more?

solutions.latex:
A speed of $2$ km/h above the limit is $62$ km/h or more.

The $z$-score of $62$ is:
$$\begin{aligned} z &= \dfrac{62 - 58}{4} \\ &= 1 \end{aligned}$$
In a normal distribution, about $68\%$ of values lie within one standard deviation of the mean. The remaining $32\%$ is split equally between the two tails, so
$$P(Z \ge 1) = 16\%$$
Number of vehicles:
$$\begin{aligned} 0.16 \times 2400 &= 384 \end{aligned}$$

6432.stem: A business produces bottles of cola whose capacity is normally distributed with a mean capacity of 600 mL and a standard deviation of 2 mL.

parts.latex: If 99.7% of bottles pass the quality control check, what limits will the volume of cola in each bottle almost certainly lie?
What percentage of bottles with cols lie between 598 mL and 604 mL ?

solutions.latex:
About $99.7\%$ of scores lie within 3 standard deviations of the mean, so between $z=-3$ and $z=3$.

Lower limit, using $z=\dfrac{x-600}{2}$:
$$\begin{aligned} -3 &= \dfrac{x-600}{2} \\ x &= 2\times(-3)+600 \\ &= 594 \text{ mL} \end{aligned}$$
Upper limit:
$$\begin{aligned} 3 &= \dfrac{x-600}{2} \\ x &= 3\times 2+600 \\ &= 606 \text{ mL} \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ \text{the limits are } 594 \text{ mL and } 606 \text{ mL}$$

meta.final_by: claude-sonnet-5-5 26 Nov (read from the worked solution)

solutions.latex:

$$z=\dfrac{598-600}{2}=-1$$
$$z=\dfrac{604-600}{2}=2$$
So the scores lie between $z=-1$ and $z=2$.

By the $68\%$ and $95\%$ rules, each half is taken on its own side of the mean.
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Percentage} &= \dfrac{68\%}{2}+\dfrac{95\%}{2} \\ &= 81.5\% \end{aligned}$$
criteria: Finds both $z$-scores and sets up the percentage, or equivalent merit

In a sample of 5000 oranges, how many would you expect to have a weight between 90 g and 165 g?

$$\begin{aligned} z_{90} &= \dfrac{90-140}{25}=-2 \\ z_{165} &= \dfrac{165-140}{25}=1 \end{aligned}$$

$$\begin{aligned} \text{Expected number} &= 0.815\times 5000 \\ &= 4075 \end{aligned}$$
